correctness.rationale: Each predecessor of a word of length n is exactly a path of n edges labeled by that word, starting from any of the four input pairs, and its last vertex is the target pair. All such finite inputs extend bi-infinitely with the observation unchanged. Successor support is correctly computed by union over each current pair and either next input bit. Empty support is not a witness and stays empty. Shortest-path search in the closed graph of at most 15 reachable nonempty supports gives exact minima; absence of a singleton in the closure proves impossibility at all lengths. A separate set-based replay reproduced the counts (24,90,72,12,4,4,50), the four extremizers, their witnesses (100101 for 37 and 164; 010010 for 91 and 218), and all 256 rows including shortest-word multiplicities and reachable-support counts. The original --csv option writes a regenerated CSV rather than checking an already packaged file in place; the independent comparison checked the actual packaged rows. This is exact finite verification, not formal certification.

value.rationale: An exact endpoint-inference cutoff and all-rule census would be a useful gap if unknown, but here the cutoff, extremizers and all length/witness data come directly from the matched existing catalogue. The additional reachable-support sizes and counts of shortest words are correct catalog fields, but the frozen result does not motivate a separate precise question about either or show why either addition is mathematically useful beyond the already-known classification. The method and replay are useful verification, not a new valuable finding as submitted.
